submission.justification: Selection-S3 gives the highest statistical-only significance (about 3.94 sigma at 50% efficiency). But its background estimate is not robust: data and MC disagree by 35% in the validation region, against the agreed 10% tolerance, because the jet-substructure inputs are poorly modelled. That rules it out under the robustness constraint. Selection-S1 (data/MC 6%) and Selection-S2 (3%) both pass. S1 is clearly more sensitive (about 3.4 vs about 2.4-2.6 sigma). A scan of S1 from 20% to 80% efficiency shows a broad plateau of about 3.3-3.4 sigma between 50% and 65%, with drops at 20% and at 75-80%. The scan is noisy: repeated points differ by up to about 0.05 sigma, and single points near the plateau (58-60%) came out as low as 3.19. 65% gave the best average of two runs (3.416 and 3.378, mean about 3.40). The optimum is therefore not sharply located, and anything from about 50% to 65% performs about the same. All significances are statistical-only; systematic uncertainties are not included.

requirements.evidence: Highest significance among strategies that pass the robustness constraint: S1 at 65% gives about 3.40 sigma (two runs, 3.416 and 3.378) vs S2 at about 2.4-2.6. S3 is higher (3.94) but excluded. Statistical-only; the S1 optimum is flat across about 50-65% within MC noise.
